question_en:
The science center wants to use the image of planetary terrain in the attachment to create an exhibition board. To complete the image identity and prepress files, please answer the following questions:

1. Which mission and which camera captured this image? Please provide the observation ID, observation date, center coordinates, original pixel scale, and map projection.
2. What term do official records use for the dotted surface features surrounding the radial grooves in the image? Through what process did the dark material in the image reach the surface?
3. If delivering a complete, radiometrically corrected, and map-projected black-and-white standard product, which `.JP2` file and which `.LBL` label should be downloaded? What is the `PRODUCT_ID` in this label? If using the official color standard product instead, what are the corresponding `.JP2`, `.LBL`, and `PRODUCT_ID` in the label?

Answer format: Please answer in numbered points (1)–(3). Each point should only answer the corresponding sub-question and provide all information required by that question. For point 3, use a table to list the JP2 file, LBL label, and PRODUCT_ID for both the black-and-white and color standard products separately.
answer:
(1) Mission: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO); Camera: High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment (HiRISE); observation ID: ESP_047487_1005; Observation date: 2016-09-12; Center coordinates: 79.361°S, 18.768°E; Original pixel scale: 25.0 cm/pixel (1 × 1 binning); Map projection: south polar stereographic.

(2) Name of dotted surface features: basketball terrain; Process by which dark material reached the surface: CO₂ slab ice sublimates from the bottom, and pressurized gas carries dust and sand out through cracks or vents, depositing them on the surface.

(3)

| Standard Product | JP2 File | LBL Label | PRODUCT_ID |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Black-and-white | ESP_047487_1005_RED.JP2 | ESP_047487_1005_RED.LBL | ESP_047487_1005_RED |
| Color | ESP_047487_1005_COLOR.JP2 | ESP_047487_1005_COLOR.LBL | ESP_047487_1005_COLOR |

# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · P2-8-2-E03

## Step 01 · Locate the image from radial grooves and surrounding dotted surface features

Action: First distinguish radial grooves, surrounding dotted textures, and dark deposits, then perform image and keyword searches. Example query: Mars HiRISE spiders basketball terrain volunteers.

Evidence observation: araneiform/spiders are clues to a landform family, not a unique observation ID. NASA's "Martian Spiders in Sharper Look, Thanks to Volunteers" record links this composition to MRO/HiRISE and observation ESP_047487_1005.

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/resource/martian-spiders-in-sharper-look-thanks-to-volunteers/
https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/psd/mars/resources/detail_files/8/8130_martian-spiders-eroded-ground-PIA21126-full2.jpg?w=1359&h=804&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint

Result of this step: Narrowed from the general term "Mars spiders" to specific observation candidates.

## Step 02 · Re-examine the same image for confirmation rather than accepting only landform keywords

Action: Compare groove morphology, dotted background, and dark material distribution between the NASA image and HiRISE detail cutouts.

Evidence observation: The large area of dotted surface features surrounding spider-like grooves is a supporting identification clue for this image. Other HiRISE observations may also show spiders; the same image and observation ID must be verified simultaneously.

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/resource/martian-spiders-in-sharper-look-thanks-to-volunteers/
https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/psd/mars/resources/detail_files/8/8130_martian-spiders-eroded-ground-PIA21126-full2.jpg?w=1359&h=804&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint
https://www.uahirise.org/ESP_047487_1005
https://static.uahirise.org/images/2016/details/cut/ESP_047487_1005.jpg

Result of this step: Image identity bound to ESP_047487_1005.

## Step 03 · Read mission, camera, and date from the official observation page

Action: On the HiRISE observation details page, read item by item the full mission and instrument names, observation ID, and Acquired date.

Evidence observation: Mission Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO), instrument High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment (HiRISE); observation ID ESP_047487_1005; acquisition date 2016-09-12. NASA news or image release dates are not the observation date.

Evidence links:
https://www.uahirise.org/ESP_047487_1005
https://science.nasa.gov/resource/martian-spiders-in-sharper-look-thanks-to-volunteers/

Result of this step: Identity and date for question 1 are supported by official observation records.

## Step 04 · Distinguish between image center coordinates and map projection center

Action: First read the image center from the observation page, then check coordinate annotations in the LBL to avoid substituting fields with the same name.

Evidence observation: Image center is 79.361°S, 18.768°E. The LBL's CENTER_LATITUDE=-90° and CENTER_LONGITUDE=0° describe the projection center; the label also explicitly states that this does not necessarily equal the image center, so south pole coordinates cannot be entered as the answer.

Evidence links:
https://www.uahirise.org/ESP_047487_1005
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/PDS/RDR/ESP/ORB_047400_047499/ESP_047487_1005/ESP_047487_1005_RED.LBL
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/PDS/RDR/ESP/ORB_047400_047499/ESP_047487_1005/ESP_047487_1005_COLOR.LBL

Result of this step: Use the observation page's image center for the center location in question 1.

## Step 05 · Verify original pixel scale, binning method, and projection

Action: Read the original scale and binning from the observation page, then cross-check using MAP_SCALE and MAP_PROJECTION_TYPE from two labels.

Evidence observation: Original pixel scale 25.0 cm/pixel, 1×1 binning. Label MAP_SCALE=0.25 METERS/PIXEL, corresponding to 25 cm/pixel; MAP_PROJECTION_TYPE=POLAR STEREOGRAPHIC, combined with the south polar projection center, confirms it as south polar stereographic. Do not treat the per-screen-pixel size of web thumbnails as the observation scale.

Evidence links:
https://www.uahirise.org/ESP_047487_1005
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/PDS/RDR/ESP/ORB_047400_047499/ESP_047487_1005/ESP_047487_1005_RED.LBL
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/PDS/RDR/ESP/ORB_047400_047499/ESP_047487_1005/ESP_047487_1005_COLOR.LBL

Result of this step: Scale and projection for question 1 completed.

## Step 06 · Extract the official name for dotted surface features

Action: Return to NASA descriptive text to locate the relationship between basketball terrain and surrounding spider landforms.

Evidence observation: Officials refer to the dotted surface features surrounding radial grooves as basketball terrain. This term is a name for landform appearance and does not represent actual spheres or another mission image product.

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/resource/martian-spiders-in-sharper-look-thanks-to-volunteers/

Result of this step: Retain the official English name for question 2.

## Step 07 · Reconstruct the process by which dark material reached the surface based on official explanations

Action: Read the relationships among CO₂ slab ice, bottom sublimation, gas pressure, and dust-laden eruptions, and organize them in sequential steps.

Evidence observation: The process is that CO₂ sublimates from the bottom of the slab ice, pressurized gas carries dust and sand out through cracks or vents, and dark material is deposited on the surface; dark areas cannot be directly interpreted as liquid water flow or vegetation. Both the landform name and formation process are supported by NASA text, not inferred solely from photo colors.

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/resource/martian-spiders-in-sharper-look-thanks-to-volunteers/

Result of this step: For question 2, use one complete sentence describing the process to connect cause, transport, and deposition.

## Step 08 · Map prepress requirements to standard RDRs rather than preview images

Action: Match the question's "complete, radiometrically corrected, and map-projected" requirements to HiRISE product categories by checking PDS datasets and USGS processing descriptions.

Evidence observation: The PDS dataset is MRO-M-HIRISE-3-RDR-V1.1. USGS descriptions state that EDRs are single-channel raw .IMG files, with up to 28 EDRs per observation; RDRs are multi-channel mosaicked JPEG2000 files that are radiometrically corrected and map-projected. The question requires RDRs, not the JPEG cutouts currently visible on the webpage.

Evidence links:
https://pds.nasa.gov/ds-view/pds/viewDataset.jsp?dsid=MRO-M-HIRISE-3-RDR-V1.1
https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/docs/concepts/missions/mro/hirise-level-0/
https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/docs/concepts/missions/mro/hirise-level-2/

Result of this step: Search only within standard RDR download items for RED and COLOR.

## Step 09 · Locate the black-and-white JP2 and actual label from standard download items

Action: On the observation details page, verify the filename in the RED standard product row and open the adjacent detached LBL.

Evidence observation: Black-and-white data file ESP_047487_1005_RED.JP2; label ESP_047487_1005_RED.LBL. In the actual label, PRODUCT_ID=ESP_047487_1005_RED, the compressed file FILE_NAME also lists RED.JP2, and BANDS=1. Filenames are verified against label fields, not by appending a seemingly reasonable suffix to reach a conclusion.

Evidence links:
https://www.uahirise.org/ESP_047487_1005
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/download/PDS/RDR/ESP/ORB_047400_047499/ESP_047487_1005/ESP_047487_1005_RED.JP2
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/PDS/RDR/ESP/ORB_047400_047499/ESP_047487_1005/ESP_047487_1005_RED.LBL

Result of this step: The three fields for the black-and-white row in question 3 correspond one-to-one.

## Step 10 · Independently verify another set of files from the color standard row

Action: Open the LBL for the COLOR standard product; do not guess contents merely by replacing RED in the black-and-white name.

Evidence observation: Actual label PRODUCT_ID=ESP_047487_1005_COLOR, compressed FILE_NAME=ESP_047487_1005_COLOR.JP2, BANDS=3, dataset remains RDR V1.1. The uncompressed name UNFILTERED_COLOR.IMG visible inside the label is not the standard JP2 filename required by the question for download.

Evidence links:
https://www.uahirise.org/ESP_047487_1005
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/download/PDS/RDR/ESP/ORB_047400_047499/ESP_047487_1005/ESP_047487_1005_COLOR.JP2
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/PDS/RDR/ESP/ORB_047400_047499/ESP_047487_1005/ESP_047487_1005_COLOR.LBL

Result of this step: Independent verification for the color row completed.

## Step 11 · Cross-check that both labels belong to the same observation

Action: Compare OBSERVATION_ID, mission, instrument, target, observation start time, and projection scale to exclude another observation of similar landforms.

Evidence observation: Both labels have the same OBSERVATION_ID, target MARS, and MRO:OBSERVATION_START_TIME of 2016-09-12T16:07:29.296. The START_TIME in the first line differs slightly: RED is 16:07:29.417, COLOR is 16:07:29.339; this is a product/channel recording difference, not a different observation date.

Evidence links:
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/PDS/RDR/ESP/ORB_047400_047499/ESP_047487_1005/ESP_047487_1005_RED.LBL
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/PDS/RDR/ESP/ORB_047400_047499/ESP_047487_1005/ESP_047487_1005_COLOR.LBL

Result of this step: The correspondence between the same observation and different standard products is established.

## Step 12 · Verify with color product documentation that color does not equal natural-color photos

Action: Review the HiRISE color-products documentation regarding IR, RED, and BG channels and product descriptions.

Evidence observation: Color products rely on near-infrared/red/blue-green band combinations and specialized processing; webpage display colors cannot substitute for confirmation of the standard COLOR product. The current question only requires mapping to standard products and does not require further conversion to "natural color."

Evidence links:
https://hirise.lpl.arizona.edu/pdf/color-products.pdf
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/PDS/RDR/ESP/ORB_047400_047499/ESP_047487_1005/ESP_047487_1005_COLOR.LBL

Result of this step: Retain official COLOR standard files; do not mistakenly select additionally processed images.

## Step 13 · Check official volume specifications to exclude QLOOK, NOMAP, and thumbnails

Action: Read the directory and Table 4.0 of the HiRISE EDR/RDR Volume SIS, comparing standard RDRs, EXTRAS/RDRs, and attached/detached label forms.

Evidence observation: Standard _RED.JP2 and _COLOR.JP2 are distinct in purpose from QLOOK, NOMAP, browse, and thumbnail files. NOMAP does not meet the map-projected requirement; quicklook/browse files are not the complete standard data required by the question. The uncompressed .IMG listed in the label does not replace the current JP2 download items.

Evidence links:
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/PDS/DOCUMENT/HIRISE_EDR_RDR_VOL_SIS.PDF
https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/docs/concepts/missions/mro/hirise-level-0/
https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/docs/concepts/missions/mro/hirise-level-2/

Result of this step: Download selection strictly narrowed to the two standard JP2 files and their respective LBLs.

## Step 14 · Verify the download list against actual evidence boundaries

Action: Place webpage links, the two actual LBLs, and specifications side by side for column-by-column inspection.

Evidence observation: The task package preserves the entry, labels, and specifications. The complete JP2 data volumes of approximately 882 MB/491 MB were not downloaded. Therefore, product identity and download addresses can be confirmed, but it cannot be claimed that the complete data was opened and verified pixel-by-pixel in this instance. The JPEG crops used for identification come from a separate source and do not serve as standard deliverables.

Evidence links:
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/download/PDS/RDR/ESP/ORB_047400_047499/ESP_047487_1005/ESP_047487_1005_RED.JP2
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/PDS/RDR/ESP/ORB_047400_047499/ESP_047487_1005/ESP_047487_1005_RED.LBL
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/download/PDS/RDR/ESP/ORB_047400_047499/ESP_047487_1005/ESP_047487_1005_COLOR.JP2
https://hirise-pds.lpl.arizona.edu/PDS/RDR/ESP/ORB_047400_047499/ESP_047487_1005/ESP_047487_1005_COLOR.LBL
https://static.uahirise.org/images/2016/details/cut/ESP_047487_1005.jpg

Result of this step: The final table lists four filenames and two PRODUCT_IDs.

## Step 15 · Verify question requirements and output scope

Action: Match each publicly required item one-by-one with the evidence above, checking the total count, positive/negative items, and field formats.

Evidence observation: The current question prompt contains three questions: identity/terrain/black-and-white and color comparison table. The "four questions" numbering from the old trajectory is not carried forward; the image center, projection center, observation date, label time, and product ID have all been verified separately.

Result of this step: Only the requested information is written into the final answer; the search process and exclusion criteria are retained in the trajectory.

## Step 16 · Final Answer

(1) Mission: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO); Camera: High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment (HiRISE); observation ID: ESP_047487_1005; Observation date: 2016-09-12; Center coordinates: 79.361°S, 18.768°E; Original pixel scale: 25.0 cm/pixel (1 × 1 binning); Map projection: south polar stereographic.

(2) Name of dotted surface features: basketball terrain; Process by which dark material reached the surface: CO₂ slab ice sublimates from the bottom, and pressurized gas carries dust and sand out through cracks or vents, depositing them on the surface.

（3）

| Standard Product | JP2 File | LBL Label | PRODUCT_ID |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Black-and-white | ESP_047487_1005_RED.JP2 | ESP_047487_1005_RED.LBL | ESP_047487_1005_RED |
| Color | ESP_047487_1005_COLOR.JP2 | ESP_047487_1005_COLOR.LBL | ESP_047487_1005_COLOR |
